glossary.nutritional deficiencies: Lack of essential nutrients such as iron, vitamins or protein.
glossary.mucosal: Relating to the inner lining of the gut.
glossary.digestive enzymes: Proteins, mainly from the pancreas, that break food into absorbable pieces.
glossary.bile salt: Substance made by the liver from cholesterol that helps break fat into tiny droplets for absorption.
glossary.ileal: Relating to the ileum, the last part of the small bowel where bile salts and B12 are absorbed.
glossary.chronic diarrhoea: Loose stools lasting more than four weeks.
glossary.pallor: Pale skin, often a sign of anaemia.
glossary.anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, causing tiredness, breathlessness and pallor.
glossary.epigastric: The upper central part of the abdomen, just below the ribs.
glossary.foreign travel: Recent travel abroad, a key clue for infections such as Giardia.
glossary.EMA: Anti-endomysial antibodies: a blood test for coeliac disease.
glossary.IgA: Immunoglobulin A: the antibody class measured in coeliac blood tests; IgA deficiency gives a false negative.
glossary.iron studies: Blood tests of iron stores and transport, including ferritin and transferrin saturation.
glossary.endoscopy: A camera passed into the gut to look at the lining and take biopsies.
glossary.gluten-free diet: A diet avoiding wheat, barley and rye, which contain gluten.
glossary.pancreatic enzyme: Enzymes such as lipase normally made by the pancreas; given as capsules when the pancreas fails.
glossary.vitamin supplementation: Giving extra vitamins by mouth or injection to correct deficiencies.
glossary.autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.proximal small bowel: The first part of the small intestine: the duodenum and jejunum.
glossary.absorptive surface area: The total area of gut lining available to take up nutrients, increased by villi.
glossary.calcium: A mineral needed for bones, absorbed in the duodenum with the help of vitamin D.
glossary.duodenal: Relating to the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine after the stomach.
glossary.jejunal: Relating to the jejunum, the middle part of the small intestine.
glossary.ADEK: The fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K, lost when fat is not absorbed.
glossary.toxin: A harmful substance made by a microorganism.
glossary.pancreatic enzyme replacement: Capsules of pancreatic enzymes taken with meals to digest fat and protein.
